role: link-weight regressor: predicts W_link (a cost, high for a bad link) from delay, loss and an inverse-bandwidth input; not a classifier, selects no algorithm

source.license: none declared in the source repository (no license file in commits a0ce0ed or 6b6c008; GitHub reports license null)
source.redistribution_permission: NOT ESTABLISHED: without a license, default copyright applies; written permission or a license from the repository owner is required before these files are redistributed
source.import: files copied byte-for-byte from the git blobs of that commit (LF line endings); not modified

feature_contract.normalization: z = (x - mean) / scale with scaler_regressor.json (StandardScaler fitted on the 2,800 training rows; population standard deviation)

inputs.delay_ms: latency (scenario mean end-to-end packet latency, ms)
inputs.inv_bottleneck_bw: 1 / max(throughput, 1e-6), throughput = scenario aggregate delivered traffic in Mb/s (a proxy, not a link capacity)

path_objective_statistics.computed_over: all 3,500 scenarios, including the 700 test rows; population standard deviation (numpy std, ddof 0)

proxy_mappings.latency_ms (used as RTT statistics): latency (one-way scenario latency, not an RTT)

known_limitations: Trained on scenario-level aggregates (whole simulated networks), not on per-link measurements; using it on links is a transfer outside the training unit.
The training inverse-bandwidth input is 1 / delivered traffic, whereas link-level inference uses 1 / available link bandwidth; same unit, different physical quantity.
The target is a deterministic function of latency, loss, jitter, queue occupancy and throughput, so the high test R2 mostly reflects that formula; inverse bandwidth has gain importance 0.004.
Predicts a weight near or below zero for low-delay, loss-free inputs (879 of the 1,000 training rows under 10 ms have target 0); W_link is floored at 0.
Path-objective statistics include the test partition and are not unbiased validation estimates.
